newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian parliament approves new first premier.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian parliament approves new first premier.

text.p: Cambodia's ousted Prince Norodom Ranariddh on Wednesday was replaced as first prime minister by Foreign Minister Ung Huot in a move that strongman Hun Sen said signalled the end of Cambodia's turmoil.
But despite the approval of parliament, Ung Huot still faced hurdles before winning full acceptance as co-premier, most notably opposition from Ranariddh's father, King Norodom Sihanouk.
Eighty-six members of the 120-seat National Assembly voted by secret ballot in favour of Ung Huot's nomination as first prime minister. A total of 99 assembly members attended the Wednesday session.
Second Prime Minster Hun Sen, who ousted Ranariddh in a bloody coup early last month, hailed the assembly's overwhelming approval of the man he backed for the job.
"The crisis is now over," Hun Sen told reporters after the session.
But members of the Cambodian opposition in Bangkok said Ung Huot's nomination was illegal and in violation of the constitution.

"The appointment today by the National Assembly, in an atmosphere of intimidation and fear, of Mr Ung Huot is totally illegal," the Union of Cambodian Democrats (UCD) opposition group said in a statement released in the Thai capital.
The newly-formed UCD is made up of members of parliament from Ranariddh's party and a smaller allied party and their supporters.

Many royalist supporters fled the country in the wake of Hun Sen's takeover and a subsequent crackdown on Ranariddh's FUNCINPEC party in which some 40 people were killed, according to United Nations human rights officials.
Ung Huot, 52, was chosen to replace Ranariddh by FUNCINPEC members who remained in the country.
Diplomats said Ung Huot's acceptance as a legitimate first premier hinged on the approval of the king.
"It's another step but more things have to be done," said an Asian diplomat. "The question is whether this is accepted by the king or not."

Sihanouk said late last month he would not recognise Ung Huot as first premier as the post belonged to his son. The king also said that a vote on a new first prime minister by an incomplete parliament would be invalid.
Hun Sen said he and Ung Huot were preparing to visit Sihanouk in Beijing where the king is receiving medical treatment.
The United States and the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) both said soon after the prince's ouster that they still recognised the prince as first prime minister.

Indonesia, whose foreign minister Ali Alatas heads a three-member mediation team on Cambodia, said on Wednesday any ASEAN comment on Ung Huot's election would have to wait for a meeting in Singapore next week.
Earlier on Wednesday, the National Assembly voted to strip Ranariddh of his parliamentary immunity clearing the way for his prosecution for alleged crimes if he returned to Cambodia.

The prince was out of the country at the time of his ouster. Hun Sen said later Ranariddh was free to come back, but that he would have to face charges for his illegal negotiations with the outlawed Khmer Rouge guerrilla group and for alleged weapons smuggling.
The prince has dismissed the accusations and called from abroad for opposition to his former co-premier and coalition partner.
Ung Huot told parliament he was honoured to have been elected first prime minister and said the main task of the government was to strengthen political, economic and social institutions.
"I am determined to try by all means to make the Kingdom of Cambodia a genuine state governed by the rule of law with strong political, legal, economic and social institutions," he told the assembly.
He also promised to work closely with Hun Sen's Cambodian People's Party in preparing for elections scheduled for May.
